findings.title: GET request is built from the full URI object instead of the request path
findings.evidence: Passing the parsed URI directly to Net::HTTP::Get.new can generate an absolute-form request target rather than the origin-form path expected by normal origin servers, causing valid HTTPS fetches to fail depending on the server/proxy path handling.
findings.recommendation: Construct the request with the path/query component, for example using 'Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.request_uri)' or an explicit request object with the correct path and headers.

findings.title: Write timeouts are not retried even though Net::HTTP can raise them on supported Ruby versions
findings.evidence: The retry list only includes open timeout, read timeout, and connection reset, so a transient 'Net::WriteTimeout' during request transmission will bypass the bounded retry logic and fail immediately on Python-supported POSIX deployments using Ruby 3.11+ Net::HTTP.
findings.recommendation: Include 'Net::WriteTimeout' in 'RETRYABLE_ERRORS' and add a test covering a transient write-timeout followed by success.
